</figure>
<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison with State-of-the-Art.</span>
We perform extensive evaluation, comparing GVDepth with SotA domain-dependent and domain-agnostic methods. Results for KITTI and DDAD datasets are shown in <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.1 Evaluation of Zero-shot Accuracy ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.
Both supervised <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>, <a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">50</a>]</cite> and self-supervised <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>, <a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">53</a>]</cite> domain-dependent methods perform well on datasets matching their training domain but overfit to environmental and geometric biases, leading to reduced accuracy in KITTI <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> DDAD transfer.
Relative depth estimation models exhibit greater adaptability across domains; however, they require ground-truth scale and shift alignment, limiting their practical applicability.
Recent zero-shot metric methods, such as ZeroDepth, UniDepth, and Metric3D, demonstrate strong generalization capabilities but rely on extensive data acquisition and large-scale training, which is not always feasible.
Furthermore, UniDepth and Metric3D suffer accuracy degradation when inferring on resolutions lower than their high-resolution training data.
While resizing and padding can address this, these adjustments increase computational demands, limiting their suitability for resource-constrained systems.
GVDepth delivers comparable results while being adaptable to arbitrary camera setups, aspect ratios, and image resolutions.
Depending on the train-test dataset combination, our method ranks first or second across most metrics, despite training on only a single dataset and using a fraction of the data required by other zero-shot MDE methods.
This is particularly impressive, as each dataset features unique environments and camera setups, demonstrating that our model relies on domain-agnostic perspective geometry cues rather than domain-specific semantic cues.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison with Ground Plane Methods.</span></p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T2" class="ltx_table">

</figure>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Our proposed <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> implicitly encodes depth of the ground plane, which has been utilized in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, <a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>, <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite> to improve MDE accuracy in autonomous driving scenes.
However, as demonstrated in <a href="#S4.T2" title="In 4.1 Evaluation of Zero-shot Accuracy ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> significantly outperforms GEDepth <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite>, with the performance gap further widened after fusion with <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>FCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>.
As we will show, the primary cause of such discrepency is inability of GEDepth to leverage vertical image positions and disentangle perspective geometry for pixels located outside the road surface.
In the Supp. materials we provide a comprehensive analysis and critique of existing models that rely on ground plane depth.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span><span id="S4.F4.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Qualitative results.</span> Predicted depths, errors and uncertanties for DrivingStereo <math id="S4.F4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> KITTI evaluation.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">In <a href="#S4.F4" title="In 4.1 Evaluation of Zero-shot Accuracy ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> we illustrate qualitative results of our DrivingStereo <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> KITTI evaluation.
Notably, it can be seen that vertical uncertainty <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{\Sigma_{Y}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>𝐘</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{\Sigma_{Y}}</annotation></semantics></math> is lower in closer regions, and decreasing with higher distances.
An interesting detail appears in the left image, where the vertical uncertainty adapts to the scene’s leftward slope, indicating that the model is aware of ground perturbations.
Additionally, in the right image, the vertical uncertainty is significantly higher for a car lacking a visible ground-contact point, creating ambiguity in its vertical image position cue.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Ablation studies</h3>

<figure id="S4.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T3.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 3</span>: </span><span id="S4.T3.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Ablation of canonical representations.<span id="S4.T3.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Baseline – standard depth regression with geometric augmentations. Focal – depth regression via Focal Canonical Transform - <math id="S4.T3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>FCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>. This is equivalent to Metric3D<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite>, but trained on our setup. Vertical – depth regression via Vertical Canonical Transform - <math id="S4.T3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>. Fusion – depth regression with model as designed in <a href="#S3.F3" title="In 3.2 Canonical Transforms ‣ 3 Proposed Method ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>. Training datasets on rows, testing datasets on columns. Best results are </span>bolded<span id="S4.T3.9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">, second best are <span id="S4.T3.9.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">underlined</span>. In-domain evaluation results are <span id="S4.T3.9.2.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">shaded</span>. </span>Note:<span id="S4.T3.9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Focal and vertical results presented here are from separate models leveraging <math id="S4.T3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext>FCT</mtext><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.T3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext>VCT</mtext><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>, not from submodels in <a href="#S3.F3" title="In 3.2 Canonical Transforms ‣ 3 Proposed Method ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.</span></span></figcaption>
<div id="S4.T3.10" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:496.9pt;height:180.6pt;vertical-align:-88.6pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-119.2pt,43.3pt) scale(0.675821620458223,0.675821620458223) ;">

</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Evaluation of Canonical Representations.</span>
In <a href="#S4.T3" title="In 4.2 Ablation studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> we report extensive evaluation results, spanning different representations and train-test dataset combinations. Moreover, in Supplementary we report qualitative results accompanying the table.
By carefully examining the results, we can draw the following conclusions: i) <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The baseline model struggles to transfer effectively to out-of-distribution data.</span>
Without the invariance introduced by canonical representations, baseline models fail to leverage diverse perspective geometries in the training data due to the ambiguities induced by depth-camera parameters entanglement; (ii) <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Vertical image position cues generalize better than object size cues.</span>
Models with our novel <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext>VCT</mtext><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> representation generally outperform <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext>FCT</mtext><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> models, except in rare cases, potentially stemming from calibration errors.
This is particularly evident with models trained on the Waymo dataset, which encounter difficulties when relying solely on object size cues.
The probable cause is that Waymo’s cameras are positioned significantly higher, causing a variation of apparent object sizes due to the change of perspective.
In contrast, vertical image position cues are more robust, implicitly encoding camera height within the representation; (iii) <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Probabilistic fusion improves generalization by integrating both cues.</span> Our fusion strategy achieves the most accurate predictions by adaptively weighting the more reliable cue.
For example, when object size cues are more accurate (<em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">e.g</em>.<span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text"></span> DDAD <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> KITTI), the model adjusts accordingly, and the same applies for vertical position cues (<em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">e.g</em>.<span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text"></span> Waymo <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> Argoverse).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2412.06080v2/resolution_decrease.svg" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:685/420;" width="685" height="420"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S4.F5.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Resolution adaptability.<span id="S4.F5.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> <math id="S4.F5.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{A.Rel}(\%)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>Rel</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo mathsize="1.110em">%</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{A.Rel}(\%)</annotation></semantics></math> of UniDepth <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite> and GVDepth as height resolution <math id="S4.F5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> decreases from base resolution 462. Computational complexity is depicted with different circle radius. GVDepth results are from DrivingStereo <math id="S4.F5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> KITTI evaluation.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Resolution Adaptability.</span>
SoTA zero-shot methods such as UniDepth <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite> and Metric3D <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite> require resizing and padding to training resolution to achieve optimal accuracy.
However, when applied to datasets like KITTI, this approach results in the model processing nearly twice as many pixels as necessary due to padding.
This significantly increases computational complexity without adding any meaningful detail to the image.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In contrast, GVDepth is designed to be fully resolution-agnostic, adapting seamlessly to the native resolution of the input image.
As shown in <a href="#S4.F5" title="In 4.2 Ablation studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, the error rate of GVDepth remains largely unaffected even as the input resolution decreases.
This feature is especially advantageous for real-time systems, where dynamically adjusting image resolution is one of the simplest and most effective ways to control computational complexity.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 4</span>: </span><span id="S4.T4.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Surround-view generalization.<span id="S4.T4.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Vertical – model with <math id="S4.T4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>. (†): Waymo surround images added to training data. UniDepth and Metric3D evaluated with original checkpoints and resolutions.</span></span></figcaption>

<figure id="S4.F6" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2412.06080v2/semantics.svg" id="S4.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:651/307;" width="651" height="307"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S4.F6.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Error per object class.<span id="S4.F6.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Vertical – model with <math id="S4.F6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>. Focal – model with <math id="S4.F6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>FCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>. All models are evaluated on DrivingStereo <math id="S4.F6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> KITTI zero-shot transfer.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Surround-view Generalization.</span> In <a href="#S4.T4" title="In 4.2 Ablation studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> we provide results for Waymo <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> DDAD zero-shot transfer for surround-view cameras. Despite the increased ambiguity and perturbations in ground regions captured by side views, our <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{VCT(\cdot)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>VCT</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{VCT(\cdot)}</annotation></semantics></math> model outperforms <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{FCT(\cdot)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>FCT</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{FCT(\cdot)}</annotation></semantics></math> on side cameras, with performance increasing after Waymo side cameras are included in training data.
<math id="S4.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{FCT(\cdot)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>FCT</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{FCT(\cdot)}</annotation></semantics></math> performs better on back camera, possibly due to the occlusion of bottom part of the image by ego-vehicle.
For unknown reasons, UniDepth <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite> failed to infer correct camera parameters for DDAD surround cameras, resulting in subpar performance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Generalization in Specific Regions.</span>
The strong quantitative generalization results of vertical position cues do not fully capture their performance.
For instance, a model with <math id="S4.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> might only perform better on road pixels due to its implicitly encoded planarity.
However, as shown in <a href="#S4.F6" title="In 4.2 Ablation studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, this is not the case: the <math id="S4.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> model exhibits accurate generalization across a wide range of object classes. The results clearly reveal major flaws in GEDepth’s <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite> performance, as it struggles to generalize beyond road-related pixels, particularly for safety-critical objects.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F7" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S4.F7.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2412.06080v2/ground_modulation.svg" id="S4.F7.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:685/670;" width="685" height="670"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F7.sf1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(a)</span> </span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S4.F7.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2412.06080v2/error_uncertainty_ratios.svg" id="S4.F7.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:685/670;" width="685" height="670"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F7.sf2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(b)</span> </span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F7.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="S4.F7.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Sensitivity analysis.<span id="S4.F7.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> All models are evaluated on DrivingStereo <math id="S4.F7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> KITTI. Histograms represent data distribution. </span>a)<span id="S4.F7.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> <math id="S4.F7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{A.Rel}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>Rel</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{A.Rel}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S4.F7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.F7.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>FCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> models depending on ground plane modulation severity. Ground plane modulation is expressed as <math id="S4.F7.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{A.Rel}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>Rel</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{A.Rel}</annotation></semantics></math> of ground depth calculated from camera parameters via <a href="#S3.E3" title="In 3.1 Depth Cues ‣ 3 Proposed Method ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and ground-truth depth of the road. </span>b)<span id="S4.F7.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Ratio of depth errors <math id="S4.F7.m13" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(\mathrm{A.Rel}(\mathbf{Z_{Y}})/\mathrm{A.Rel}(\mathbf{Z_{F}}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>Rel</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐙</mi><mi>𝐘</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>Rel</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐙</mi><mi>𝐅</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathrm{A.Rel}(\mathbf{Z_{Y}})/\mathrm{A.Rel}(\mathbf{Z_{F}}))</annotation></semantics></math> and uncertainties <math id="S4.F7.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbf{\Sigma}_{Y}/\mathbf{\Sigma}_{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Y</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Z</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbf{\Sigma}_{Y}/\mathbf{\Sigma}_{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> depending on depth bin.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Moreover, we examine the effects of ground plane inconsistencies and perturbations on the depth estimation accuracy.
A reasonable assumption would be that the <math id="S4.SS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> model is more sensitive to these perturbations.
However, <a href="#S4.F7.sf1" title="In Figure 7 ‣ 4.2 Ablation studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7(a)</span></a> illustrates that error for both models increases in similar pattern as ground perturbation increases.
This indicates that our <math id="S4.SS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> model can adapt and recognize perturbations which are present in the training data, atleast to the similar degree as competing methods.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, in <a href="#S4.F7.sf2" title="In Figure 7 ‣ 4.2 Ablation studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7(b)</span></a> we analyze the errors and uncertainties of both cues across discrete depth bins.
As shown, the error ratio skews towards <math id="S4.SS2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> in regions closer to the camera, which is expected.
As depth increases, the object size cue becomes more accurate due to the reduced reliability of the vertical position cue at mid-range distances.
However, for farther distances, <math id="S4.SS2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> once again achieves lower error.
We hypothesize that this is because <math id="S4.SS2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> implicitly encodes the horizon level, aiding depth estimation for distant objects.
Additionally, the estimated uncertainties follow a similar pattern, demonstrating the effectiveness of our adaptive fusion module.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Conclusion and Future Work</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We present GVDepth, a novel MDE model designed for accurate zero-shot transfer across diverse environments and camera setups, with a focus on autonomous vehicles and mobile robotics. Leveraging the fixed camera-to-ground geometry in such platforms, we introduce a <em id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Vertical Canonical Representation</em> that uses known ground depth to enforce perspective invariance, resulting in enhanced learning and generalization.
Our architecture further adaptively fuses depth estimates from object size and vertical image position cues, guided by uncertainty.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Extensive ablations across five autonomous driving datasets show that our method generalizes significantly better than object-size-based baselines, matching or surpassing state-of-the-art zero-shot models, while using only a single training dataset and far fewer computational and data resources.
Future work will explore scaling to multi-dataset training toward a foundation model for MDE in autonomous driving and mobile robotics.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p3.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="S5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:144%;">Supplementary Material </span></p>
</div>
<div id="S5.2" class="ltx_logical-block">

<figure id="S5.F8" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8: </span><span id="S5.F8.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Qualitative ablation.</span> Predicted depths and errors for DrivingStereo <math id="S5.F8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> {KITI, Waymo, DDAD} models. Baseline – standard depth regression with geometric augmentations. Focal – depth regression via Focal Canonical Transform - <math id="S5.F8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>FCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>. This is equivalent to Metric3D<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite>, but trained on our setup. Vertical – depth regression via Vertical Canonical Transform - <math id="S5.F8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>. Fusion – depth regression with uncertainty-based fusion model.</figcaption>
</figure>
    
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">F </span>Qualitative Results</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Qualitative results for different model configurations are shown in <a href="#S5.F8" title="In 5 Conclusion and Future Work ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>. All models demonstrate comparable capabilities in reconstructing semantic objects, effectively capturing object boundaries and overall scene layout. However, error maps reveal that the Baseline model struggles to handle the domain gap introduced by varying camera parameters in the zero-shot transfer setting, leading to reduced accuracy. Both the Focal and Vertical models perform reasonably well across most image regions, though they exhibit noticeable modeling errors in certain areas. In contrast, the Fusion model attains the highest accuracy by adaptively integrating the depth predictions from both Focal and Vertical models.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">G </span>Additional Ablations with Ground Plane Methods</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Additional Results.</span>
<a href="#S7.T5" title="In G Additional Ablations with Ground Plane Methods ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> presents a more detailed ablation study of GEDepth <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite>, incorporating results from additional training datasets. GVDepth consistently outperforms GEDepth across multiple training-test dataset combinations.
We do not report results on Argoverse and DDAD datasets, as GEDepth failed to achieve satisfactory convergence. We will provide further comments on this issue below.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Furthermore, in <a href="#S7.T6" title="In G Additional Ablations with Ground Plane Methods ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, we provide results for PlaneDepth <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite> and GroCo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>, which utilize the ground plane constraint in a similar manner as GVDepth. Since these methods are self-supervised, we retrained PlaneDepth with supervision, using the same backbone as our method. The results suggest that the performance gap is not due to difference in supervision or model complexity, but due to the superior out-of-distribution generalization of our approach. For GroCo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>, we report the results from the original paper, as it lacks the open-source code implementation. However, GroCo is fundamentally a self-supervised version of GEDepth <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite>, preserving all of its core principles.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Our main argument is that none of these methods are explicitly designed to enhance generalization or facilitate training with diverse perspective geometries. Moreover, they improve performance only for road pixels, unlike the proposed <math id="S7.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> that exploits the ground plane constraint for all objects.
In the following sections, we provide an in-depth analysis, offering insights into the generalization and convergence challenges faced by this methods.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.T5" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S7.T5.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 5</span>: </span><span id="S7.T5.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Comparison with GEDepth <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite>.<span id="S7.T5.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> All models are trained with equivalent setup and model complexity on KITTI, DrivingStereo and Waymo datasets. Best results are </span>bolded<span id="S7.T5.8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">, second best are <span id="S7.T5.8.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">underlined</span>. In-domain evaluation results are <span id="S7.T5.8.2.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">shaded</span>.</span></span></figcaption>

<td id="S7.T6.6.1.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t">30.28</td>

</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S7.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Detailed Analysis.</span></p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2412.06080v2/gedepth.png" id="S7.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_portrait" style="aspect-ratio:685/1132;" width="685" height="1132" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S7.F9.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="S7.F9.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Different approaches for incorporation of ground plane constraint.<span id="S7.F9.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
In our approach, <math id="S7.F9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> serves as a <span id="S7.F9.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">point of disentanglement</span>, which enables learning of <span id="S7.F9.7.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Vertical Canonical Representation</span> that is invariant to specific perspective geometry. Linear combination used in GEDepth and GroCo does not hold such properties, leading to limited generalization.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S7.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We start with the following premises, which differentiate the proposed <math id="S7.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> from aforementioned approaches:</p>
<ol id="S7.I1" class="ltx_enumerate ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S7.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(i)</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike GEDepth and GroCo, which utilize the ground plane constraint only for road pixels, the proposed canonical representation enables utilization of vertical image position cue for all objects in the scene;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(ii)</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Similarly, in constrast to GEDepth and GroCo, our approach is inherently modeled to enable perspective geometry disentanglement for all objects, resulting in better out-of-distribution generalization.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="S7.p5.2" class="ltx_p">While our extensive evaluation confirms this, here we also provide insights into why GEDepth and GroCo fail to generalize across all objects in the scene.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Both GEDepth and GroCo formulate the problem of depth regression <math id="S7.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D}\in[0,D_{max}]^{H\times W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐃</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D}\in[0,D_{max}]^{H\times W}</annotation></semantics></math> as a linear combination of the known ground depth <math id="S7.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D_{G}}\in[0,D_{max}]^{H\times W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐃</mi><mi>𝐆</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D_{G}}\in[0,D_{max}]^{H\times W}</annotation></semantics></math> and the learnable residual depth <math id="S7.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D_{R}}\in[0,D_{max}]^{H\times W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐃</mi><mi>𝐑</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D_{R}}\in[0,D_{max}]^{H\times W}</annotation></semantics></math>, weighted by the learnable <span id="S7.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">“ground attention”</span> <math id="S7.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{A}\in[0,1]^{H\times W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐀</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{A}\in[0,1]^{H\times W}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S7.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D}=\mathbf{A}\odot\mathbf{D_{G}}+(1-\mathbf{A})\odot\mathbf{D_{R}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐃</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐀</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊙</mo><msub><mi>𝐃</mi><mi>𝐆</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐀</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊙</mo><msub><mi>𝐃</mi><mi>𝐑</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D}=\mathbf{A}\odot\mathbf{D_{G}}+(1-\mathbf{A})\odot\mathbf{D_{R}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.p6.2" class="ltx_p">Through a straightforward analysis, we can notice why this formulation enhances depth estimation for road pixels only.
First, any part of the scene appearing above the horizon can not benefit from the induced perspective geometry constraint, as <math id="S7.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D_{G}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐃</mi><mi>𝐆</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D_{G}}</annotation></semantics></math> is invalid for those regions of the image.
Moreover, ground attention <math id="S7.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐀</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{A}</annotation></semantics></math> is usually estimated with the <math id="S7.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Sigmoid}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Sigmoid</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Sigmoid}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>, which has a natural tendency to converge to either 0 or 1 during optimization, leading to <math id="S7.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐀</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{A}</annotation></semantics></math> effectively being equivalent to road segmentation, as visualized in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>, <a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite>.
Even for rare cases where this is not the case, the resulting linear combination has an ambivalent geometric interpretation chosen arbitrarily by the model.
Our proposed <math id="S7.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> is a simple and elegant solution for all of these issues; it enables effective utilization of the ground plane constraint for all image regions while preserving a clear geometric interpretation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The same fundamental principles can be applied to perspective geometry disentanglement. While <math id="S7.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D_{G}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐃</mi><mi>𝐆</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D_{G}}</annotation></semantics></math> clearly disentangles depth from camera parameters, the estimated <math id="S7.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D_{R}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐃</mi><mi>𝐑</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D_{R}}</annotation></semantics></math> does not hold such properties, inducing generalization errors due to the ambiguity of depth and camera parameters.
Since the final depth <math id="S7.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐃</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D}</annotation></semantics></math> is calculated as a linear combination, it is only fully disentangled where <math id="S7.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐀</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{A}</annotation></semantics></math> is 1, which is valid only for road pixels.
On the other hand, <math id="S7.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> is inherently designed to incorporate perspective geometry disentanglement, regardless of the specific image region.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GEDepth Convergence Issues.</span>
GEDepth optimizes <math id="S7.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐃</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D}</annotation></semantics></math> from <a href="#S7.E9" title="In G Additional Ablations with Ground Plane Methods ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> without additional regularization factors or external segmentation modules, claiming that the learned attention map can automatically separate ground and other regions.
Unfortunately, in our experiments this occurred rather inconsistently, and the learned attention map converged to adequate ground segmentation only on the 19th training experiment.
In most cases, the model resorted to estimating <math id="S7.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{A}=\mathbf{0}^{H\times W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐀</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>𝟎</mn><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{A}=\mathbf{0}^{H\times W}</annotation></semantics></math>, thus ignoring the provided ground plane information and resulting in <math id="S7.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D}=\mathbf{D_{R}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐃</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝐃</mi><mi>𝐑</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D}=\mathbf{D_{R}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Final Remarks.</span>
We conducted a thorough evaluation that highlights the extremely limited generalization capabilities of models that rely on ground plane constraints <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, <a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>, <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>. While one might assume that these issues arise from limited reproducibility or incorrect convergence, the analysis we presented in previous sections suggests that the root cause lies in inherent design choices. These models are optimized to perform well only on narrow training distribution. Even within these constraints, improvements in accuracy are confined to road pixels, which are of limited relevance for safety-critical applications. In contrast, the proposed <math id="S7.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> elegantly addresses all these limitations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S8" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">H </span>Model Architecture</h2>

<div id="S8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we employ a fully convolutional encoder-decoder architecture with skip connections.
While vision transformer (ViT)-based encoders, such as DINOv2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>]</cite>, often achieve superior accuracy, their advantages typically rely on large-scale training.
A similar fully convolutional design is adopted in Metric3D <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite>, demonstrating the effectiveness of such models for generalizable monocular depth estimation (MDE).
Given our focus on single-dataset training, we prioritize convolutional backbones to reduce computational complexity while maintaining robust generalization performance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Decoder Architecture Details.</span>
Our decoder is designed similarly as in Metric3D <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite>, consisting of four blocks that progressively upsample and fuse encoder features from a resolution of <math id="S8.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\frac{H}{32},\frac{W}{32})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mfrac><mi>H</mi><mn>32</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>W</mi><mn>32</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\frac{H}{32},\frac{W}{32})</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S8.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\frac{H}{2},\frac{W}{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mfrac><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\frac{H}{2},\frac{W}{2})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Decoder channels dimensions are <math id="S8.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{756,512,256,128\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>756,512,256,128</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{756,512,256,128\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Our fusion module processes <math id="S8.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\frac{H}{2},\frac{W}{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mfrac><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\frac{H}{2},\frac{W}{2})</annotation></semantics></math> resolution feature maps <math id="S8.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐅</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{F}</annotation></semantics></math> with two compact U-Net-like networks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>, each containing 3 downsampling and upsampling blocks, producing two final feature representations.
These feature representations are processed with two convolutional blocks which predict our canonical representations <math id="S8.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbf{C_{F}},\mathbf{C_{Y}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐂</mi><mi>𝐅</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐂</mi><mi>𝐘</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbf{C_{F}},\mathbf{C_{Y}})</annotation></semantics></math> and accompanying uncertainty estimates <math id="S8.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbf{\Sigma_{F}},\mathbf{\Sigma_{Y}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>𝐅</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>𝐘</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbf{\Sigma_{F}},\mathbf{\Sigma_{Y}})</annotation></semantics></math>.
After uncertainty-based fusion, final depth map is bilinearly upsampled to <math id="S8.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(H,W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(H,W)</annotation></semantics></math> resolution.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S8.F10" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2412.06080v2/vertical.png" id="S8.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:685/151;" width="685" height="151" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S8.F10.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span id="S8.F10.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Vertical Canonical Representation regression.<span id="S8.F10.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Visualization of regression boundaries of proposed <span id="S8.F10.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Vertical Canonical Representation.</span> We predict vertical image position of ground plane projection in range <math id="S8.F10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,y_{MAX}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,y_{MAX}]</annotation></semantics></math>. Image is </span><span id="S8.F10.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">virtually extended</span><span id="S8.F10.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> beyond bottom boundary to enable depth estimation for pixels with ground-plane projection below camera field-of-view. For stability reasons, regression is bounded to <math id="S8.F10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{MAX}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{MAX}</annotation></semantics></math>, which corresponds to <math id="S8.F10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{MAX}=80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{MAX}=80</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S8.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Vertical Canonical Representation details.</span>
For convenience, we restate the equation used in Vertical Canonical Transform <math id="S8.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext>VCT</mtext><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S8.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S8.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=\frac{f_{y}h}{\left(H-c_{y}-y\right)\cos(\theta)-f_{y}\sin(\theta)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=\frac{f_{y}h}{\left(H-c_{y}-y\right)\cos(\theta)-f_{y}\sin(\theta)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S8.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Upon closer inspection, it becomes evident that mapping <math id="S8.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y\mapsto d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\mapsto d</annotation></semantics></math> can lead to unstable training if not properly regularized. Specifically,
at <math id="S8.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> corresponding to the horizon level of a given camera setup, the depth <math id="S8.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> approaches infinity.
Furthermore, for any <math id="S8.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> above the horizon, the depth <math id="S8.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> becomes negative.
To address this, as visualized in <a href="#S8.F10" title="In H Model Architecture ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>, we bound the regression of <math id="S8.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S8.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{MAX}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{MAX}</annotation></semantics></math>, derived from the inverse mapping from <math id="S8.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{MAX}=80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{MAX}=80</annotation></semantics></math>.
Additionally, to accommodate depth regression for objects with ground-plane projections below the camera’s field of view, we <span id="S8.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">virtually extend</span> the image. In practice, this corresponds to increasing <math id="S8.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> in <a href="#S8.E10" title="In H Model Architecture ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> accordingly.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S9" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">I </span>Model Complexity</h2>

</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <a href="#S9.T7" title="In I Model Complexity ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> we present the architectural details of the models used in this work.
While most results align with expectations, there are a few notable outliers worth discussing.
First, ZeroDepth exhibits the highest inference times, despite utilizing the least complex backbone among all methods.
Essentially, ZeroDepth shifts complexity from the pre-trained backbone to its proprietary self-attention layers in the decoder.
This trade-off limits its ability to fully leverage the benefits of large-scale pretraining, which may explain its subpar accuracy compared to UniDepth, Metric3D, and GVDepth, even though it uses significantly more data during training.</p>
</div>
<div id="S9.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.p2.1" class="ltx_p">On the other hand, Metric3D achieves remarkably low latency in depth prediction despite employing a relatively complex backbone.
This efficiency likely stems from predicting depths at a reduced <math id="S9.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\frac{H}{4},\frac{W}{4})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mfrac><mi>H</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>W</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\frac{H}{4},\frac{W}{4})</annotation></semantics></math> resolution, which is subsequently upsampled to the original resolution
Lastly, GVDepth stands out for its lightweight design and low inference time, even though it uses a relatively complex backbone.
Its impressive generalization performance is attributed to our novel methodology rather than reliance on model or data scaling.
In future work, we will investigate more complex transformer architectures, which were costly to train on our current computational setup.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S10" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">J </span>Ablation of Fusion Strategy.</h2>

<div id="S10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <a href="#S10.T8" title="In J Ablation of Fusion Strategy. ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> we examine the efficacy of different fusion strategies.
Zero-shot transfer results demonstrate that our adaptive fusion weighted by aleatoric uncertainties leads to superior generalization performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S11" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">K </span>Dataset Details</h2>

<div id="S11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we use KITTI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite>, DDAD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>]</cite>, DrivingStereo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite>, Waymo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite> and Argoverse Stereo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite> datasets, both for training and evaluation.
For KITTI dataset, we evaluate all models on commonly used Eigen split <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite> with Garg crop <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, resulting in 23158 training images and 652 testing images.
On DDAD dataset we use the official training and validation split, with 12650 and 3950 images, respectively.
Since Waymo, DrivingStereo, and Argoverse Stereo are not widely used for MDE evaluation, we simplify the process by creating custom dataset splits. The resulting training splits consist of {156K, 168K, 5K} samples, while the corresponding testing splits contain {5K, 5K, 500} samples, respectively.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S12" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">L </span>Camera setup calibration</h2>

<div id="S12.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S12.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we provide additional details about our camera calibration procedure.
Our proposed Vertical Canonical Transform <math id="S12.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext>VCT</mtext><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>, as indicated in
<a href="#S8.E10" title="In H Model Architecture ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>, requires the knowledge of camera parameters <math id="S12.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mathcal{C}}=\{f_{y},c_{y},h,\theta\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mathcal{C}}=\{f_{y},c_{y},h,\theta\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Here, for all datasets, <math id="S12.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{y}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S12.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{y}</annotation></semantics></math> are usually known up to the reasonable error induced by the calibration procedure.
However, for certain datasets, camera height <math id="S12.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> and camera pitch <math id="S12.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> are either unknown, or not properly calibrated.
To remain consistent throughout this work, we recalibrate the extrinsic parameters for each dataset, with details provided in <a href="#alg1" title="In L Camera setup calibration ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="alg1" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">
