            Run semantic segmentation model on <math id="alg1.l5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> to acquire road pixels <math id="alg1.l5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>

<table id="S12.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 11: </span><span id="S12.F11.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Calibration histograms.</span> Height and pitch histograms acquired by calibration procedure described in <a href="#alg1" title="In L Camera setup calibration ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. Best viewed zoomned in.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S12.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S12.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S12.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Calibration results.</span>
Estimated camera height <math id="S12.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> and camera pitch <math id="S12.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> for each dataset are provided in <a href="#S12.T9" title="In L Camera setup calibration ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>.
Moreover, in <a href="#S12.F11" title="In L Camera setup calibration ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> we visualize the histograms obtained with our calibration procedure.
Since DrivingStereo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite> and KITTI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite> do not report extrinsic parameters, we use the estimated values in our proposed canonical transform.
Furthermore, for the DDAD dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>]</cite>, we observe a significant discrepancy between the official and estimated extrinsics.
Therefore, we use our calibrated parameters, as they align more closely with the ground-truth depth.
In contrast, for Argoverse Stereo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite> and Waymo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite>, the estimated values are consistent with the official calibration.</p>
</div>
<div id="S12.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S12.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S12.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">KITTI Calibration Issues.</span>
We would also like to address the problems with KITTI calibration. As shown in <a href="#S12.F11" title="In L Camera setup calibration ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>, the pitch histogram for the KITTI dataset does not follow an unimodal distribution.
We believe that this highlights inconsistencies in the official KITTI intrinsics calibration across different recording sequences.
While this observation is not novel <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, it is rarely, if ever, discussed in the context of MDE.
Given that the KITTI dataset remains a cornerstone for MDE evaluation, we believe that this issue should be given increased attention.</p>
</div>
<div id="S12.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S12.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S12.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Evaluation with Per-frame Calibration.</span></p>
</div>
<figure id="S12.T10" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S12.T10.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 10</span>: </span><span id="S12.T10.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Evaluation with per-frame extrinsics calibration.<span id="S12.T10.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Vertical – depth regression via Vertical Canonical Transform - <math id="S12.T10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>. <td id="S12.T10.8.1.8.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">3.28</td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.8.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r">92.7</td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.8.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;"><span id="S12.T10.8.1.8.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">2.78</span></td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.8.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;"><span id="S12.T10.8.1.8.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">1.61</span></td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.8.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;"><span id="S12.T10.8.1.8.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">99.6</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S12.T10.8.1.9" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S12.T10.8.1.9.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_r">Fusion</th>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.9.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">6.96</td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.9.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">3.17</td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.9.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r">92.7</td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.9.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;"><span id="S12.T10.8.1.9.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">3.01</span></td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.9.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;"><span id="S12.T10.8.1.9.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">1.76</span></td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.9.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;"><span id="S12.T10.8.1.9.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">99.5</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S12.T10.8.1.10" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S12.T10.8.1.10.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb ltx_border_r">Fusion+</th>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.10.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S12.T10.8.1.10.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">6.85</span></td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.10.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S12.T10.8.1.10.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">3.15</span></td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.10.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_r"><span id="S12.T10.8.1.10.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">92.7</span></td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.10.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;"><span id="S12.T10.8.1.10.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">2.91</span></td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.10.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;"><span id="S12.T10.8.1.10.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">1.74</span></td>
<td id="S12.T10.8.1.10.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;"><span id="S12.T10.8.1.10.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">99.6</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S12.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S12.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Our per-frame calibration procedure offers potentially higher accuracy than median-filtered results.
This is because it better captures ground plane perturbations and vehicle dynamics, which cause slight variations in camera pitch. In <a href="#S12.T10" title="In L Camera setup calibration ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>, we present evaluation results using per-frame calibration.
While this approach leads to slight performance improvement, the gain is marginal, possibly due to the noise in our calibration process.
Although such additional information about vehicle dynamics and perturbation could theoretically be integrated into a real system using localization with visual odometry or sensor fusion, we exclude these results from the main paper since competing methods do not leverage this information.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S12.F12" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2412.06080v2/height.svg" id="S12.F12.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:685/433;" width="685" height="433"></object></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2412.06080v2/pitch.svg" id="S12.F12.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:685/433;" width="685" height="433"></object></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S12.F12.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 12</span>: </span><span id="S12.F12.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Calibration sensitivity.<span id="S12.F12.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Sensitivity to Gaussian noise perturbations in extrinsic parameters evaluated on KITTI dataset. Vertical – depth regression via Vertical Canonical Transform - <math id="S12.F12.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>. Fusion – depth regression with fusion model. Train/test dataset combination for both models is DrivingStereo <math id="S12.F12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> KITTI.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S12.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S12.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S12.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Calibration Sensitivity.</span>
Models involving canonical mapping via <math id="S12.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> are inherently sensitive to inaccuracies in camera extrinsic parameters.
In <a href="#S12.F12" title="In L Camera setup calibration ‣ GVDepth: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation for Ground Vehicles based on Probabilistic Cue Fusion" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>, we evaluate the <math id="S12.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{A.Rel}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>Rel</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{A.Rel}</annotation></semantics></math> metric for our Vertical and Fusion model configurations under varying levels of Gaussian noise in the extrinsic parameters.</p>
</div>
<div id="S12.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S12.p8.1" class="ltx_p">While both models exhibit sensitivity to calibration noise, the Fusion model demonstrates a smaller error increase due to its uncertainty-based fusion with depth from <math id="S12.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>FCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>.
However, the Fusion model’s error still increases under noisy conditions, indicating that its uncertainty prediction does not fully compensate for inaccuracies in camera calibration.
This is expected, as camera calibration directly affects the canonical mapping performed by <math id="S12.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> and is not internally estimated by the model.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S13" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">M </span>Additional Considerations</h2>

<div id="S13.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S13.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S13.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multi-dataset Training.</span>
Almost all challenges in multi-dataset training for MDE arise from inconsistent and ambiguous perspective geometries, making our approach inherently scalable due to the invariance introduced in canonical spaces.
While we lacked the computational resources to scale the training to the level of a MDE foundation model, in Tab. 3 in main text we demonstrated our method’s ability to leverage diverse perspective geometries in the training data induced by geometric augmentations, especially compared to the <span id="S13.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Baseline</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S13.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S13.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S13.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Flat Ground Assumption.</span>
Our method implicitly assumes the ideal ground plane within the <math id="S13.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>VCT</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCT}_{\bm{\mathcal{C}}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Unlike in GEDepth <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite>, which explicitly models the ground slope, we choose to grant the model greater flexibility.
Motivation behind this choice is straightforward; our proposed canonical transformation is designed to assist the model in resolving ambiguities that diverse training data alone cannot, such as the entanglement of depth and camera parameters.
For other adversarial perturbations, like ground plane imperfections, we do not explicitly model them.
Instead, we allow the model to internally adjust values in canonical space when it detects these perturbations within highly diverse training data.
Moreover, the uncertainty-based fusion provides the model with additional capabilities to adaptively weight cues based on aleatoric uncertainty, enabling the down-weighting of specific cue in highly uncertain regions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S13.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S13.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S13.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Acknowledgment.</span> This research has been funded by the H2020 project AIFORS under Grant Agreement No 952275.</p>
</div>
</section>

              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
